shortName: University of Kansas School of Medicine

medSchoolStudLife.diversity: The University of Kansas and the School of Medicine believe the intentional creation of a diverse learning environment is essential to achieving their educational missions. Diversity and quality in medical education and health care delivery are ensured through programs that recruit, enroll, and graduate a diverse population of students; train culturally competent physicians; recruit a diverse faculty; institutionalize measures that develop and retain minority academic physicians; and expand research on health care issues affecting disadvantaged and under-served populations.
medSchoolStudLife.leaveOfAbsence: A medical student may request a leave-of-absence for a maximum of twelve months for medical, personal, or academic (e.g., fellowship or research) reasons.  The LOA must be approved by the Associate Dean of Student Affairs or the Academic Committee.  Except for students who are in the combined MD/PhD program, graduation requirements must be completed within six years of the date of matriculation.
medSchoolStudLife.organizationActivities: Students on all campuses are assigned to an academic society.  These learning communities foster a collegial learning environment through student/faculty and student/student interactions across the four medical classes. Societies also provide a structure for student advising, promote a sense of community for students and faculty, and encourage the development of professional attitudes and behaviors. In addition to academic societies, students have ample opportunity to serve in a variety of leadership positions within more than 50 student organizations that promote cultural diversity, special interests, academic specialties, and community service.  Student-created and student-run JayDoc Free Clinics are invaluable to the patient populations they serve. An on-campus, 50,000 square-foot fitness center provides the full range of opportunities for individual and group fitness activities. Students also have access to Jayhawk sporting events held on the undergraduate campus in Lawrence.
medSchoolStudLife.setting:
Each of our campuses offers a unique environment, providing diverse experiences to meet students' needs and preferences.

Kansas City: Located at the vibrant 39th Street West district and historic Westport intersection, the campus is steps from the Country Club Plaza. The city features a renowned parks system, live music venues, athletic events, and an array of visual and performing arts, offering an energetic urban lifestyle.

Salina: This central Kansas city blends small-town charm with big opportunities. With 51,000 residents, Salina boasts eight museums, 23 parks, four golf courses, and over 240 civic clubs. Its arena hosts exciting events, creating a dynamic community.

Wichita: A diverse city in south-central Kansas, Wichita is known for its affordability, safety, and ease of navigation. A four-time All-American City, it offers a vibrant mix of cultural experiences and modern amenities, making it an ideal setting for students to excel academically and socially.
medSchoolStudLife.housing: Affordable off-campus housing is readily available in Kansas City, Salina, and Wichita.
medSchoolStudLife.supportSystems: As part of our Core Values, the University of Kansas Medical Center is committed to creating and maintaining a diverse and inclusive learning and working environment that nurtures the growth and development of our students, faculty, staff and patients. Through various resources, training and networking opportunities, KUMC seeks to create an atmosphere of inclusion and affirmation for LGBTQIA+ individuals. Find more information here: https://www.kumc.edu/school-of-medicine/office-of-student-engagement/student-programs/medical-school-students/student-diversity-organizations.html
medSchoolStudLife.wellnessPrograms:
We encourage students to develop and maintain a balanced approach to life. These resources are promoted through programs and events on campus that cover the cultural, emotional, intellectual, physical, social and spiritual dimensions of wellness. 
https://www.kumc.edu/academic-and-student-affairs/departments/office-of-student-life/programs-and-resources/student-wellness-program.html
medSchoolStudLife.campusCulture: Our three campuses reflect the diverse and inclusive culture of Kansas, offering opportunities to thrive academically, socially, and personally. Each campus is uniquely tailored to meet students’ needs, fostering a strong sense of community and engagement. The Kansas City campus offers an energetic urban environment surrounded by cultural and recreational opportunities. Fostering a vibrant campus culture enriched by the city’s parks, live music, athletic and art venues. The Salina campus combines small-town charm with big opportunities. The city offers access to cultural, recreational, and civic activities. The Wichita campus blends the resources of a large city with a sense of affordability and accessibility, making it a dynamic place to live and learn. Students benefit from the vibrant cultural experiences and modern amenities Wichita offers, encouraging a strong sense of belonging for students pursuing their medical careers.

medSchoolCurriculum.dressCode: There is no formal dress code. In cases where students are functioning as medical professionals, either with clinical patients or simulated patients, dress must be appropriate and professional.
medSchoolCurriculum.tutoringPrograms: Each student works with Academic Society directors and assistant directors, who serve as PBL facilitators, academic coaches, and advisors.
medSchoolCurriculum.patientInteraction: ACE provides early, longitudinal exposure to patients and health care systems via ongoing experiences that have learners performing as physicians-in-training beginning in the first month of year one.
medSchoolCurriculum.instructionStyle: ACE curriculum components: active/self-directed learning (flipped classroom, Big Case, PBL, CBCL); lectures; clinical skills; simulation; learning communities; assessment/documentation/coaching
medSchoolCurriculum.clinicalRotations: Six eight-week third-year clerkships are patient-population based (e.g., Care of the Adult; Infant/Child/Adolescent Health) and are offered across Kansas hospitals and clinics.
medSchoolCurriculum.curricularHighlights: The ACE (Active, Competency-based, Excellence-driven) curriculum prepares patient-focused, teamwork-oriented, population-minded physicians to provide expert, professional and compassionate care for individuals, groups and diverse communities.  ACE prepares independent and reflective lifelong learners who will succeed in the next stage of medical education and who are equipped for lasting commitment to self-improvement in practice.  The curriculum develops learners who are confident and comfortable with the use of health care technology and who can critically evaluate the appropriate and effective use of new technologies.  ACE helps learners develop exemplary skills in patient safety, performance improvement, and patient-centered team care.  The curriculum also educates learners with a broad understanding of the health care system.
medSchoolCurriculum.primaryCarePrograms: With more than 40% of its graduates entering primary care residencies, KU continues its longstanding commitment to training physicians who will provide comprehensive healthcare for their patients. Because Kansas is largely a rural state, many of KU's efforts focus on rural medicine, beginning at the premedical level with the Scholars in Rural Health Program. Medical student courses include the required senior-year Rural Preceptorship focusing on rural primary care, the option to complete a portion of the required third-year clerkships at rural sites, and an elective course offered during the summer between years one and two that provides students with early exposure to rural medicine and primary care research. Related student organizations include very active rural medicine and family medicine interest groups. Medical Education Network Sites are an integral part of the School of Medicine's mission to implement rural health initiatives throughout the State of Kansas.
medSchoolCurriculum.researchPrograms: MD/PhD Physician Scientist Training Program: After the second year of medical school, students perform research within the laboratories of medical center faculty and complete requirements for a PhD prior to returning to complete their MD training. Research opportunities are available in anatomy/cell biology, biochemistry, microbiology, pathology, pharmacology/toxicology, physiology, and the Neuroscience Graduate Program. In addition, MD/PhD students may choose to study bioengineering, in which some of the research and training may take place on the Lawrence campus.  Students are given tuition and stipend support throughout the program. The Summer Research Training Program is a summer program in which students earn elective credit and can compete to earn stipend support. The Post-Sophomore Fellowship in Pathology provides a highly flexible year of research and clinical training. Participants receive a stipend and support for educational expenses.
medSchoolCurriculum.communityServiceText: Without requirement, a large majority of KU medical students choose to be very active in their respective campus communities, as well as on a national and global level.
medSchoolCurriculum.researchThesisText: Multiple programs and opportunities are available throughout the academic year and during summers for students who wish to conduct research or participate in other scholarly activities.
medSchoolCurriculum.affiliatedHospitals: U of Kansas Hosp; KC VA Med Ctr; Colmery-O'Neil VA Med Ctr; Eisenhower VA Med Ctr; Children's Mercy Hosp; Providence Med Ctr; Salina Regional Health Ctr; Via Christi Regional Med Ctr; Wesley Med Ctr
medSchoolCurriculum.gradingSystem: Competency-based assessment. Pass/Fail in years one and two; pass with distinction/pass/fail in year three.  Graduation with Honors designation available.

medSchoolInformation.generalInformation: Since the establishment of the University of Kansas School of Medicine in 1905, its students and faculty have built upon a tradition of excellence.  Innovative education and training equips graduates with the ability to deliver highly competent and compassionate patient care. Through exceptional medical education, patient care, service, and research, the medical faculty and staff are dedicated to preparing students for the future of medicine.
medSchoolInformation.missionStatement: To improve lives and communities in Kansas and beyond through innovation in education, research and health care.

medSchoolApplication.letterGuidance: We request letters from a variety of sources --  faculty, employers, supervisors, or other persons who know you well and can be regarded as objective evaluators.
medSchoolApplication.typicalInterviewDay: All 2025-26 KU SOM interview days will take place virtually. Interviewees will receive access to a private site with interview day information: the admissions process and timelines, financial aid information, presentations from our Office of Student Engagement, and education deans. Additionally, interviewees will be invited to attend virtual Q&A sessions with current medical students. On-campus Second Look Days will be offered for all three campuses, and final dates will be sent to applicants who are interviewed.
medSchoolApplication.interviewFormat: Two individual 30-minute interviews, one open-file with a committee member. All interviews will take place virtually.
medSchoolApplication.ctsRequired: Kansas residents and nonresidents with strong Kansas ties receive highest priority.  International students are not considered.
medSchoolApplication.acceptOutstateApplInformation: The University of Kansas is a state-supported institution that gives primary consideration to Kansas residents and those with strong ties to Kansas.
medSchoolApplication.acceptCanadianApplInformation: Applicants are only considered who are citizens or permanent residents of the United States, or have an approved status due to Deferred Action for Childhood Arrivals (DACA).
medSchoolApplication.acceptInternationalApplInformation: Applicants are only considered who are citizens or permanent residents of the United States, or have an approved status due to Deferred Action for Childhood Arrivals (DACA).
medSchoolApplication.dacaDetail: An applicant who is not a citizen must submit a photocopy of his or her permanent resident visa card or DACA approvals.
medSchoolApplication.additionalInfo:
The University of Kansas is a state-supported institution that gives primary consideration to Kansas residents and applicants with strong ties to the state of Kansas.

While we will only accept candidates who are academically qualified to meet the intellectual rigors of a medical career, our focus on out-of-state applicants is to select those who will contribute to the depth and breadth of backgrounds and life experiences of the entering class. We carefully consider those personal characteristics deemed necessary to develop into a highly competent and compassionate physician. We seek applicants who have a sound awareness of issues in medicine and who have demonstrated their commitment to serve others.

Please review the University of Kansas School of Medicine website for updated admission policies and information.
medSchoolApplication.mcatScoresAdditionalInfo: The admissions committee will consider the highest MCAT total from a single test date less than three years old.
medSchoolApplication.mcatScreenAdditionalInfo: Any applicant with less than a 496 MCAT or below will not be reviewed.
medSchoolApplication.gpaScreenAdditionalInfo: Any applicant with less than a 3.3 BCPM GPA will be reviewed to identify factors that warrant additional review or consideration for interview. Only courses from a college or university accredited by the Council for Higher Education Accreditation (CHEA) will be calculated in the GPA.
medSchoolApplication.minUndergradGpaInfo: The committee will see the GPA by academic year. In addition to undergraduate GPA, the committee will consider any postbacc or graduate coursework. GPA trends are more important than the individual grade.
medSchoolApplication.minCreditHourInfo: All coursework will be considered, there is no minimum number of hours in order to consider postbacc or graduate coursework.
medSchoolApplication.courseworkAcceptanceInfo: All coursework from from a college or university accredited by the Council for Higher Education Accreditation (CHEA) will be considered, community college coursework is accepted. Courses taken to meet the biology and chemistry prerequisites must be courses required of science majors.
medSchoolApplication.letterOfIntentAdditionalInfo: Letters of intent or interest are not accepted. However, any applicant granted an interview may submit one application update that may include any relevant changes or updates to experiences, qualifications or grades since the initial application submission.

medSchoolFinancial.financialAid: The Student Financial Aid Office provides financial assistance to students in the form of grants, scholarships, loans, and work.  Students should complete the FAFSA to be considered for any federal or need-based financial assistance.  Funds come from many sources, including the institution, federal government, the State of Kansas, and the KU Endowment Association.  Of special note is the Kansas Medical Student Loan program (KMSL), which is only available to students attending the University of Kansas School of Medicine.  This program provides full tuition plus a monthly stipend of $2000 to selected students who agree to enter a primary care residency and then work in underserved areas in Kansas.  Students who fulfill the terms of the Kansas Medical Loan Program are not required to repay the KMSL funds received.
medSchoolFinancial.tuitionPolicy: Tuition and fees are assessed semi-annually every fall and spring for the four years of the regular MD curriculum.  Non-resident rates apply to non-residents for tuition purposes.  Tuition and fees are subject to change without notice from the Kansas Board of Regents.

medSchoolAcceptance.waitlistProcedure: One waitlist, with applicants notified of numerical position on list.  Applicants are offered admission when there is a seat available.

medSchoolSelection.premedReqRec:
Students who develop skills for identifying their gaps in knowledge and the sources of information necessary to fill those gaps are better prepared for learning in the ACE curriculum.
https://www.kumc.edu/school-of-medicine/academics/degree-programs/md-program/admission-and-aid/premedical-requirements.html
medSchoolSelection.oldestPrereqDate: There is no oldest date requirement for prerequisite coursework. All prerequisite coursework will be considered.
medSchoolSelection.selectionFactors: Applicants are encouraged to submit their AMCAS applications by September 1. Qualified Kansas residents receive strong first preference for interview and admission; successful nonresident applicants will have significant Kansas ties and/or add breadth to the class. Academic performance, MCAT scores, application materials, letters of recommendation, impressions gained from interviews, and nonacademic experiences are assessed throughout the admissions process. Transfer applications from students currently enrolled in good standing in an LCME-accredited medical school are considered only if a position is available in the third-year class; when space is available, Kansas residents with a compelling need to transfer receive priority.
medSchoolSelection.preMedShadowText: Applicants are expected to have a general understanding of healthcare and medicine based upon shadowing, volunteer, and/or employment experiences. Although a specific number of hours is not required, applicants are encouraged to invest the time needed to acquire knowledge of the roles of members of the healthcare team, as well as an understanding of the meaning of working with patients and serving them as a physician.
